bull.b: Growing quarterly revenue alongside a substantial booked order base provides tangible visibility into near-term demand. Continued adoption of SteraMist and a rising open order book can support sustained expansion over the next several quarters if execution remains consistent.

Consumables add a recurring, usage-linked revenue stream to equipment sales, while stronger gross margins and lower expenses improve operating leverage. This combination can make growth more durable and help narrow losses as the installed base expands.

Additional regulatory approvals broaden the addressable applications and geographies for TOMI’s technology. New patents may also strengthen differentiation, supporting longer-term commercial expansion across food safety, healthcare, life sciences, and institutional markets.

bear.b: TOMI has not yet converted revenue growth into sustainable profitability or internally generated cash. Persistent cash consumption can constrain investment in sales, regulatory work, and operations while increasing the company’s dependence on external financing.

High leverage relative to equity reduces financial flexibility and leaves less capacity to absorb execution setbacks. Combined with deeply negative returns on equity, the balance sheet may limit funding choices and increase pressure to raise capital on unfavorable terms.

Important elements of the company’s growth and strategic plans depend on financing and approvals that are not yet certain. Delays or failure in these milestones could defer revenue opportunities, increase costs, and prolong reliance on capital markets while losses continue.
